Present appeal is filed by the appellant - ONGC under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act (hereinafter be referred to as "the Act") and under Section 96 of the Civil Procedure Code NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5060/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined for quashing and setting aside the impugned judgment and award dated 21.01.2008 passed by the learned 9 th Additional Senior Civil Judge, Mahesana (hereinafter be referred to as "the Reference Court") in Land Acquisition Reference Case No. 111 of 2004 whereby the trial Court has allowed the reference and awarded additional compensation at Rs.31.00 per square meter over and above the amount of compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

2. Facts of the present case, in nutshell, are as under:-
2.1

The land situated at Village: Telavi, Taluka and District:
Mehsana were acquired for drillsite No. NKIS Project for which notification under Section 4 of the Act was published on 30.12.1996 and declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published on 11.12.1997.
The Land Acquisition Officer, after issuing notice and hearing the claimants, has passed an award awarding compensation of Rs.3.00 per square meter.

2.2 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimants have preferred aforesaid Reference before the Reference Court claiming compensation at the rate of Rs.190/- per square meter.

The Reference Court concluded that the market value of the land was Rs.34/- and therefore the claimants were entitled to additional compensation at Rs.31/- per squire meter (Rs.3.00 +
Rs.31.00 = Rs.34.00) with solatium at 30%, additional market value @ 12% and interest at 9% p.a. from the date of taking possession till one year and thereafter at 15% p.a. till its realization on all amounts.
NEUTRAL
CITATION

undefined
3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Reference Court, the appellant has preferred the present appeal.

4. Heard Mr.Ajay Mehta, learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. Ashok Prajapati, learned counsel for the respondents - claimants and Ms. Krishna Desai, learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondent - State of Gujarat.
5. Mr.Mehta, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the Reference Court has committed an error in coming to the conclusion that the claimants would be entitled to additional amount of compensation at Rs.31/- per square meter.
He would submit that the Reference Court has erred in considering the excessive market value of the land since no such market value existed in and around the area under acquisition.

He would submit that the notice under Section 9(3)(4) of the Act was served upon the claimants, however, they have not produced any documents with regard to the higher valuation and, therefore, the acquiring authority has decided the representation and General Manager- Oil & Naturalgas ... vs Prahladji Gamaji Thakoe on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158907944/
2 closed the proceedings under Section 25(2) of the Act and awarded Rs.3.00 per square meter to the claimants under Section 11 of the Act.

sentences.text: He would submit that the Reference Court has committed an error in awarding solatium at 30% and interest at 12% and appreciating the fact that LAQ Officer has fixed the land value after considering the land prices of the area and sale deeds of contemporaneous period.
He would submit that the Reference Court has committed an error in awarding the additional compensation and, therefore, the interference is required to be called for.

He would submit that the appeal NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5060/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
10/06/2025 undefined deserves to be allowed and the impugned judgment and award deserves to be modified.
6. Mr.Prajapati, learned counsel for the claimants would submit that the Reference Court has not committed any error in awarding additional compensation.

He would submit that no interference is required to be called for and the appeal being meritless deserves to be dismissed.
7.
This Court has considered the submissions canvassed by learned counsel appearing for the respective parties and considered the material on record and gone through the impugned judgment and award.

8. The Reference Court has considered relevant factors which are discussed in para - 15 of the impugned judgment and award wherein the Reference Court has considered the value rise in the market value on the basis of the decision of this Court in the case of Special Land Acquisition Officer Vs. Motibhai Mohanbhai reported in 1997 (2) GLH 773.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition Officer Vs. Motibhai Mohanbhai reported in 1997 (2) GLH 773
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid observation made by the Reference Court, this Court is in complete agreement with the findings recorded by the Reference Court in para - 15 and, therefore, no interference is required to be called for in the present appeal.

9. That the claimants had placed the evidence on the point of potentiality of their land inter alia stating that their land is having irrigation facilities for which revenue abstract is put on record.
Hence, it is required to be discussed the potential evidence in detail.

That Village Santhal and Dhanpura (Katosan) is nearby NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5060/2008 JUDGMENT DATED:
10/06/2025 undefined and having a common boundary, which fact was admitted by witness examined on behalf of respondent - ONGC.

Looking to the documents / decisions at Exhibit 11, 12 and 13 wherein the market value is assessed at Rs.57.00 per square meter and as said decisions have not attained finality, which are under challenge, the same cannot form sole base for awarding additional compensation in the application, however, it transpires from the decision at Exhibit 13 that in the said application, one of the claimant has produced documentary evidence in the form of sale instance of Village : Santhal adjoining village having common boundary, from which it established and the Court has arrived at conclusion that the market value of land situated at Village ;
Santhal as on 30.04.1986 was Rs.16.47 per square meter.

That in absence of rebuttal evidence on this count by the otherside, this court cannot completely ignore the same, though the same is highly disputed and objected by the otherside, however, in my opinion, the said documentary evidence can be adopted as base for fixation of market value of the land under reference is as on 30.04.1986.
In the reference notification is dated 30.12.1996, thus, there is a clear time gap of 10 years and 08 months.
The market value of the land was determined to extent of Rs.16.47 per square meter.

Considering the time gap of 10 Years and 08 Months the claimants are entitled to get Rs. 34.03 as market value as against that they have been paid Rs. 03.00 per square meter

,
therefore, the claimants are clearly entitled to get additional compensation of Rs. 31.03 per square meter, which can be NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/5060/2008 JUDGMENT DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined rounded of as Rs.31.00 for the sake of convenience.

10. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and considering the aforesaid observations made by the Reference Court, this Court is in complete agreement with the findings recorded by the trial Court and, therefore, no interference is required to be called for.
The appeal being meritless deserves to be dismissed and accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

If the amount of compensation is not deposited by the appellants, the same shall be deposited before the concerned Court within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the order of this Court.

After deposit of the amount of compensation, the same shall be disbursed in favour of the claimant/s through RTGS, after proper verification along with the interest and solatium as awarded by the Reference Court.
Registry is directed to transmit back the record and proceedings of the case to the concerned Court forthwith.
There shall be no order as to costs.
